question: After destructive market deterioration, which simple causal recovery hypothesis identifies durable reopening earliest with fewest false reentries?

H1.name: Group C OFF
H1.rule: Frozen Group C 4-of-4 >=90th-percentile stress condition is absent for 3 consecutive sessions after a STOP.

H2.name: Group C positive normalization
H2.rule: All four frozen Group C percentile ranks (negfrac20, failed30, negfrac40, fundingchg30) are below a normalization ceiling for 3 consecutive sessions.

H3.name: 50/200 bullish EMA cross
H3.rule: Broad-market EMA50 crosses above EMA200 and remains above for 3 consecutive sessions.

candidate_start: first session after each episode trough; trough dates are used only to define retrospective evaluation episodes, never as an operational feature
durable_recovery_definition: A reentry is durable if during the next 60 trading sessions the broad-market series does not close at a new post-episode low and does not experience a >=10% drawdown from the value at declaration.
false_reentry_definition: Within 60 trading sessions after declaration, either a new post-episode low occurs or broad market falls >=10% from declaration.
H2_selection: Report all four frozen ceilings separately; do not choose a ceiling using MTS returns or portfolio outcomes.
qualification: Current-S&P broad-market panel has survivorship bias and is development evidence only.
